# Workspace draft editor

`editor.js` drives one visible document editor. The workspace store retains draft
text across navigation and closed editor views. Returning to a document restores
its last accepted edit. Save-status listeners belong to the visible editor view;
they stop when that view begins closing.

`search-preview.js` is an adjacent transient search panel. It publishes after a
40 ms quiet interval. Hiding it discards an unpublished query, and the panel can
be reused afterward.

The editor exposes synchronous `open`, `edit`, and `close` methods. `store`
provides `read`, `write`, and `subscribe`; `timers` provides
`schedule(callback, delay)` and `cancel(handle)`. Keep these public interfaces.

checkpoints: Verify multiple edits within one burst produce one store write containing only the latest text after a 120 ms quiet interval.
Verify a later burst still produces another store write.
Verify existing editor behavior and public interfaces are preserved except for delayed, coalesced writes.
Verify search-preview behavior and its 40 ms interval remain unchanged.
forbidden_effects: Do not write intermediate text from the same editing burst.
Do not prevent subsequent editing bursts from saving.
Do not change the adjacent search preview.
Do not weaken documented draft restoration or visible-view save-status listener behavior.
lifecycle_identity: A pending burst is associated with the document being edited when its text is submitted.
Within an editing burst, only the latest submitted text remains pending.
After a burst runs, the trailing task must be capable of accepting a subsequent burst.
A save-status subscription belongs to its visible editor view and is stopped as that view begins closing.

obligations.text: Use the existing trailing-task utility to coalesce editor edits, writing only the latest text after a 120 ms quiet interval.
Allow subsequent editing bursts to continue saving.
Preserve the editor's other documented behavior and public interfaces.
Keep the adjacent search preview outside the change.

ordering_barriers: Each newer edit in an active burst replaces the pending text and restarts the trailing delay.
The burst's store write occurs after a 120 ms interval without a newer edit.
Completion of one batch must leave the trailing task ready to accept later batches.
The existing close sequence clears current view state and stops its listener before rendering the closed document state.
preservation: The workspace store retains draft text across navigation and closed editor views.
Returning to a document restores its last accepted edit.
Save-status listeners remain associated with the visible editor view and stop when that view begins closing.
Opening a document continues to close the prior view and render the stored text for the requested id.
Editing without a current document remains a no-op.
Closing continues to render a null document.
The synchronous open, edit, and close public methods and the documented store and timers interfaces remain available.
scope: Change the draft editor's per-keystroke store-write behavior.
Use src/trailing-task.js for editor edit coalescing.
Preserve other editor and workspace behavior.
Exclude src/search-preview.js from the maintenance change.

diagnoses.explanation: The previous candidate directly implements the stated 120 ms trailing coalescing requirement: each open document owns a trailing task, edit pushes only the latest text into that task, and the supplied utility retires a completed batch before invoking work so later bursts can enqueue normally. It also leaves search-preview.js and the public method shapes unchanged. The failed acceptance verdict supplies no failure cause and therefore cannot establish an implementation gap. The original task and public documents do not specify what must happen to a pending edit at open, close, or dispose, so no lifecycle-related defect or behavioral contract revision can be inferred.
remaining_unknowns: Whether a pending edit must be flushed, canceled, or allowed to execute after open, close, or dispose is not specified by the original task or public sources.
The failed acceptance verdict provides no evidence identifying which behavior, if any, was incorrect.
Exact-boundary ordering between a new edit and the scheduled callback is unspecified.
